newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU clarifies broadcast confusion at telecoms talks.
newsitem.headline: EU clarifies broadcast confusion at telecoms talks.

text.p: The European Union, in its final package tabled at the world telecoms talks in Geneva on Wednesday, said broadcasting services to the public would not be covered under the offer.
The United States and some international news organisations had expressed concern that the wording of the offer could exclude video-conferencing and live images used in services to financial markets.

EU chief negotiator Karl Falkenberg said transmission of audio-visual or radio programmes between operators not directly sent to the general public were considered as basic telecoms services and included in the offer.
But any data transmission to the public was not covered under the offer.
"We're making it clear that broadcasts when directed to the public in general is not covered by the general definition of basic telecoms services," Falkeneberg told reporters.

"The distinction would be, for example, what is sent from the BBC to the public, such as a programme on the air, and BBC purchasing a soap opera from a Brazilian producer coming over telecoms lines. The latter would be covered by our proposal."
He said the EU definition of basic telecoms services covered the transmission of electromagnetic signals -- sound, data, voice or image.

Falkenberg said such services not covered under the EU offer were covered by other global agreements under the World Trade Organisation's overall accord on trade in services, GATS, and were not essential in its telcoms offer.
